budget.usage.lede: Spend and outcomes over the last 7 days.
budget.usage.plan.title: Plan budget
budget.usage.plan.description: Your plans’ usage windows, as Claude Code and Codex report them on each run
budget.usage.plan.none: Shows each account’s usage windows after its next Claude Code or Codex run.
budget.usage.stop.title: Automations stop at
budget.usage.stop.description: Check-ins, triggers, goal rounds and agents’ own follow-ups wait once an account passes this much of a window, and go on after it resets. What you start always runs
budget.usage.stop.own: Its own line. Same follows Automations stop at
budget.usage.pane.lede: Spend and outcomes over the last 7 days.
budget.usage.subagents.title: Subagents run on
budget.usage.subagents.description: Claude Code’s own subagents (Explore, Plan, page reads) and workflow agents. They run on the task’s model unless you pick one here; an agent that names its own model keeps it. Where it went shows what they took
budget.usage.drain.title: Drain watch
budget.usage.drain.description: Warns here, and on your phone when it’s set up, when an account’s last two hours of runs took twice or more its usual share of a window for the same work. Copy report puts the numbers in words for a support ticket
budget.usage.notice.hide: Hide until this window changes again
budget.usage.live.title: Check Codex while work waits
budget.usage.live.description: While work waits for a Codex plan, wisp asks Codex every 10 minutes how its windows stand (nothing is spent). A reset that comes early, like a banked one, lets that work go at once
budget.usage.hold.title: Ask near the limit
budget.usage.hold.description: Before a task would take a 5-hour or weekly window past this, wisp asks first. Scheduled runs and crew jobs wait in Needs you
budget.usage.wait.title: Wait for the reset
budget.usage.wait.description: At a usage limit, the task waits under Scheduled and carries on in the same conversation when the window resets. Off: it stops and asks you
budget.usage.charts.title: Charts and breakdowns
budget.usage.charts.description: Per day, per project and per harness · model
budget.usage.stop.codex: Its own line. From December, Plus, Pro and Business plans share one allowance across ChatGPT and Codex: a lower line here leaves room for your chats. With a line set, wisp asks Codex how its windows stand before an automation starts if the last reading is over 15 minutes old (nothing is spent)
budget.usage.spare.title: Spare allowance
budget.usage.spare.description: When a weekly window resets within a day with a fifth or more left, home says so and offers that account. wisp never switches for you
budget.usage.notices.title: Window changes
budget.usage.notices.description: When a plan’s usage window appears, goes, changes its length or moves its reset, a line here and on home says so until you hide it. wisp never switches for you
budget.spare.tip: Resets {when}. What’s left then doesn’t carry over. wisp never switches accounts for you.
budget.spare.label: {left}% of {whose} left, resets {when}
budget.view.title: Usage
budget.view.unpricedNote: Codex, Cursor, Antigravity and Copilot report tokens but not cost (Copilot bills in premium requests), so their turns count in turns and outcomes but not in spend.
